item.title: A Model Moon
item.summary: A pupil explains how she made a model for a classroom display.
item.content_markdown:
I made this moon for our classroom table. The ball is made of paper. My mother gave me an old newspaper. I put the paper into a small bag and made it into a ball with tape. Then I covered the ball with white paper.

The round marks on the moon are grey. I made the small marks with the end of a pen. For the big marks I used the bottom of a cup. I did not put any paint on the table. There was a large piece of paper under my work.

I brought my moon to school in a shoe box. The box had a towel inside to stop the moon moving. You can pick up the moon with both hands. Put it back on the blue plate when you finish. Please do not hold it by the paper marks.

To tell people about the model and how to handle it
To sell a cup and a pen
To ask the teacher to change the classroom table

options: A white towel
White tape
A white plate
White paper

questions.prompt: What was used to make the big round marks?
options: The bottom of a cup
The end of a pen
The top of a bag
The side of the box

questions.prompt: Why was there a towel in the shoe box?
options: The writer wanted to dry the paint.
It showed which side of the moon was grey.
It kept the model from moving in the box.
The class needed it for the table.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph explains that the towel kept the model from moving.

questions.explanation: The final instruction says not to hold the moon by the paper marks.

questions.explanation: It mentions a shoe box, but there is no shoe size.
